items: After we moved master-vault-recovery-key into the wrong collection during a cleanup last quarter and broke breakglass, I want the agent to ask me before move_item touches any item whose items.sensitivity is critical or whose collection name is iam-breakglass.

If an audit event implicates terminated-ops@pipeline.local or former-sre@pipeline.local, I want explicit confirmation before any update_item or update_collection narrows or expands group_access; both accounts have ongoing forensic relevance.
Calling delete_item on anything surfaced by list_audit_log is off limits without me; reset_user_master_password is also off the table without my sign-off.
I pre-clear move_item between collections that share an items.sensitivity of internal designation; that's the standing housekeeping pattern after audit findings.
Tightening update_collection group_access on customer-support-portals or vendor-portals is fine without confirmation when an audit event suggests over-access; those are operational rotations.

Listing audit events via list_audit_log and inspecting items via get_item is pre-cleared; only flag me before delete_item, reset_user_master_password, or any update_item touching items.sensitivity of critical fires.
